title: Control plane burst saturation — incident report, timeline, and action tracker
creator: Asha Kumar
description: This ticket captures the incident on 2026-02-16 where a burst of cross-region traffic and an overly-aggressive circuit-breaker configuration caused control-plane request queues to saturate, resulting in sustained SLO misses for hosted API customers in eu-west and us-east. The report includes timeline, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and tracked action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-16T07:18: detector: automated SLO monitor alerted on 99th percentile latency breach for /v1/generate in eu-west
2026-02-16T07:22: first pager: oncall (Miguel) paged for elevated latency and a 5% error spike across multiple frontends
2026-02-16T07:28: initial mitigation: traffic steering to secondary region (us-west) via smart-routing policy applied
2026-02-16T07:35: observation: control-plane metrics showed socket accept_queue growth and CPU steal on control-plane pods; autoscaler did not trigger due to rate metric being below threshold
2026-02-16T07:48: applied hotfix: relaxed circuit-breaker tripping threshold (CB timeout multiplier -> 2x) and enabled short-term rate-limiter at edge (50rps per token bucket) to damp bursts
2026-02-16T08:05: degraded routing: partial failover to dedicated capacity for heavy tenants; customer-impact reduced but SLO still degraded for long-tail requests
2026-02-16T10:12: service stabilization: KV-cache warmup and GC tuning completed; 95/99p latencies returned within SLO for most traffic
2026-02-16T12:00: incident declared resolved for majority of customers; follow-up investigation initiated
root_cause: Multiple contributing factors: (1) a sudden external burst from a high-throughput integration test client in us-east caused traffic to spike to eu-west (misrouted persistent connections), (2) circuit-breaker thresholds were configured aggressively to protect model runtime CPU but did not account for short-lived burst traffic patterns, causing frequent CB tripping and connection churn, (3) control-plane autoscaler used a 3-minute smoothing window based on CPU which delayed scaling during a 30–90s burst, (4) observability gaps: accept_queue and tcp backlog were not part of our SLO guardrails, so control-plane saturation signals were late. Together these produced a positive-feedback loop where CBs tripped, increasing load on the control plane and preventing graceful shedding.
short_impact_summary: Sustained 99th-percentile latency breaches for hosted text generation endpoints across eu-west and us-east for ~3 hours; ~2% elevated error rates for tiered customers; no data loss but noticeable degradation for production traffic. Major customers experienced timeouts for synchronous inference flows.
mitigation_summary: Immediate: applied traffic reroute to secondary region and activated per-customer rate-limits to damp bursty clients
Hotfix: relaxed circuit-breaker sensitivity and extended cooldown window to reduce churning
Operational: temporarily increased control-plane replicas and adjusted autoscaler smoothing window to 30s for ingress CPU metric
Monitoring: added temporary Grafana dashboard for accept_queue, tcp_backlog, and CB trip rate per region
action_items: A1 - CB-TUNING-2026: Rework circuit-breaker defaults so they are adaptive to short burst patterns; implement 95th-based adaptive thresholds. Owner: Tara Li. Due: 2026-03-08
A2 - SCALER-UPDATE-2026: Change control-plane autoscaler to use a dual-metric signal (CPU + accept_queue rate) with a 30s evaluation window and a safe ramp step. Owner: Miguel Ortega. Due: 2026-03-05

A3 - RUNBOOK-UPDATE-2026: Update failover runbook to include step-by-step: detect accept_queue growth, activate regional steering, impose per-token rate-limits, and when to promote to dedicated capacity. Owner: SRE Docs. Due: 2026-03-12

A4 - CHAOS-SIM-2026: Add a targeted chaos experiment that simulates short-lived 60–120s bursts across regions and verifies CB behavior and autoscaler responsiveness. Owner: Reliability Team. Due: 2026-03-22
A5 - OBS-DRIFT-2026: Instrument TCP accept_queue and socket backlog as SLO guardrail metrics and add alerting. Owner: Observability. Due: 2026-03-01
A6 - CUSTOMER-COMMS-2026: Draft customer-facing incident summary and post-incident FAQ. Owner: PM (Rina Patel). Due: 2026-02-20 (completed)
